(Sorry AFK, someone just came to the door BRB)

When Shoga was found to have the 'gift' of magic, the clan thought she was destined to make the clan great.  But, when her magic turned wild and more times than not caused disaster, the clan named her "Cursed Doom Bringer" and as soon as they could, exiled and left her to die.  Instead, she survived. 
   For the past few years she has been wandering the wilderness shunning human, hobgoblin/goblin tribes and clans alike.  However, she did maintain a hovel and maintained a bit of a presence as the hermit living at the fringe of the village commons.  She would occasionally make trades, but remained haunted by her past looking at her magic gift with wonder and grief as it does grant her power, but she is also haunted by waking dreams where other beings seem to whisper to her.
  All was not to be as Shoga wound up being found out.  The local magistrate determined that Shoga while "civilized" for a Hobgoblin was still a danger.  So she was given a choice of either migrating to the Island of Roanoke or worse, the least of which living like an animal in a cage.  Shoga chose migrating figuring that maybe she could make a place for herself, or at least make her own path in the new lands.
   
    Shoga is a bit short for a Hobgoblin.  Often she is mistaken for a warrior or rogue because of the way she carries herself.
     She stands about 5 ft 2 inches and weighs about 167 lbs.  Her black hair is typically braided or shaved to keep it out of her way.  Perhaps a mark of the wild magic gift is that her skin tone is pale blue unlike the norm for Hobgoblins which ranges from russet to deep red.  However, what is most striking and unsettling is Shoga's, focused yellow eyes for those unused to her presence.

When Toruv was very young his family was traveling. The caravan they were a part of was beset by raiders and he was stolen along with most of the caravan’s goods. The last he saw of his family was when caravan guards were dragging them to safety. He does not remember where he was journeying to, nor where he was coming from. He was sold shortly after to a rich merchant who thought having an “elephant boy” serve tea would make his social events the talk of the town. Toruv was not a servant, and no amount of beating would force him into it. As he got larger and was better able to fight back, the merchant sold him to a fighting guild.

As a new member of the guild, he had access to training, lodging, and all the food he could eat. But even better, the guild was able to give him the family he had lost. Foes in the ring were brothers and sisters out of the ring. The training was hard but as each fighter was an investment the goal was to keep them alive and train them to be successful. Death happened in the ring, but it was not the goal. Toruv was content for the first time in his life. Thoughts of his old life grew distant.

Members of the guild do earn gold for their work. Once Toruv earned enough to cover the costs of his ‘investment’ he kept on fighting and saved his coin. For as the guild traveled the fighting circuit, he occasionally met other Loxodons. They told him of his culture, his heritage, and were themselves curious as to how one of their own ended up as a gladiator, fighting for sport and money. Toruv realized he was not like other Loxodons. 

As years stretched into decades he trained, fought and saved. Until finally one day he made enough to book passage to a new world, and maybe a new life. Leaving his second family was the hardest thing he has ever done. But he is determined to see more of the world, especially a new world.

A delegate from the Order of Kairo: "Ladies and Gentlemen, when my journey began, I was living in an ordinary world. I was an Ordinary person without much in my pockets but a dream. Do you remember this dream? The dream of a British Empire upon which the sun would never set? This dream sailed through my dreams, and it was like a call to see the world. A call I thought I could heed. But these long 20 years, as you well know, have been filled with a doldrum of progress. The Atlantic is uncrossable by conventional means. A blockade of monstrously gigantic creatures, each able to summon forth the power of an iceberg seemingly at will. Well folks, I will level with you… it's a call I considered refusing, but my mentor told me that if I want something bad enough, I have to fight for it, you have to think around it! Now, several waiters will begin passing out glasses of champagne, so please refrain from drinking it until the end. Now where was I? Ah yes... So I did!
